Historically, small and mid-cap stocks have outperformed large caps - from 1989-2024, mid-caps returned $3,000 on $100 invested versus $1,700 for large caps, though with higher volatility. However, this risk/reward dynamic has changed: large cap valuations are now at historically high levels (as high as after the dot-com bubble) while volatility has actually reversed, with large caps now more volatile than small caps. The market value concentration in large caps is at its highest since the dot-com era due to mega-cap companies going public at trillion-dollar valuations rather than growing over time.
buys.cautions: Small cap investing is more aggressive and risky long-term due to inherent volatility of smaller companies. This should not be a core holding like an S&P 500 index fund, but rather a diversification satellite position to reduce concentration in mega-cap tech stocks.
